focusedAudit.reason: 0.6.93 is a patch-lane release and carries no 0.x.0 audit attestation. The decision is recorded deliberately because two candidates were considered. (1) The Direct Files page-creation admission path — the default write path — changed, but as the continuation of the already-audited Direct Files regression program rather than a new subsystem, and it lands with a covered regression row whose fail-before is proven plus a follow-up commit correcting the admission regressions review found in it. (2) Startup progress/recovery is a genuinely new interaction surface, but it is read-only diagnosis plus three navigational actions and one explicit managed-to-Direct return that reuses the existing audited path; it introduces no new write path. Experimental managed storage remains off by default. Neither meets the introduces-or-substantially-rewrites bar, so no focused change-cluster audit was run.

items.text: **The built-in Guide is now a real manual rather than a feature tour.** Thirteen new pages cover the journeys people actually arrive with — bringing an existing Logseq graph in, where things are, capturing and planning a day, finding and revisiting, researching a document, keeping context visible, structuring repeated information, extending Tine, and what platforms exist — alongside precise reference pages for journals/tasks/scheduling, pages/links/references/search, files/external edits/backups, troubleshooting and recovery, and platforms and mobile. The index is grouped into Start, Workflows, Feature reference and Feature showcase, and every page is a read-only page in your own graph that you can copy into it. Every claim was reread against the shipped UI at the end, which is where several long-standing wrong labels and one round-trip overclaim were found and corrected.

docs.reason: This item IS the documentation change: thirteen new canonical Guide pages plus a restructured index, each registered in GUIDE_TEMPLATES with a semantic registration/link/copy test, and the single-source demo output regenerated from them. Phase D reread every claim against shipped source and corrected the wrong labels it found.

items.text: **Opening a graph now tells you what Tine is doing, and offers a way out when it cannot finish.** A progress card names the current phase and elapsed time once startup takes longer than a moment. items.text: **Indenting, outdenting and moving a multi-block selection no longer floods the undo history or the store.** Indent and outdent now apply as one shared-store command instead of one per block, and a run of Up/Down moves collapses into a single undo unit that closes on an idle pause, a three-second maximum, a change of selection, any other edit, or a reload — so one Undo reverses the move you just made rather than one block of it. A feed-spanning selection that includes a read-only day is still refused without dirtying either page.

docs.reason: Undo granularity for an already-documented operation. The Guide does not promise per-block undo units for indent, outdent or move, so no page makes a claim this contradicts.

items.text: **Creating a page in Direct Files no longer stalls and then refuses the save on a large graph** (part of GH #249, GH #266 and GH #267). The creation path ran the managed-storage shadow-import capture twice, retaining and parsing every graph file before it could answer whether one filename was safe. On affected graphs that ended in `precheck.limit`, stranded the new edit, and made graph transitions or close wait behind repeated failed flushes. Creation now checks one non-retaining streaming census—without applying the retained-shadow cumulative-byte ceiling—against the already parsed, generation-current Direct Files index and passes that single proof to the no-replace publisher. Creation still refuses an existing target, portable case/NFC aliases of that target (including ancestor directories), semantic owners, hard links, symlinks, and external creator races without overwriting their bytes; existing exact-target saves retain their prior path-local traversal behavior.

docs.reason: Restores the documented Direct Files creation behaviour rather than changing it; Reference/Files, external edits, and backups already states the save and no-replace contract that now holds again.
